newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch agency mulls launch of new DTC programme.
newsitem.headline: Dutch agency mulls launch of new DTC programme.

text.p: The Agency of the Dutch Ministry of Finance said on Thursday it was mulling the launch of at least one new Dutch Treasury Certificate programme (DTC).
"The announcement of a new DTC issue can be expected within weeks," said the Agency.
DTC programmes are short-term borrowing instruments of the Dutch government.
The Agency said it was currently preparing estimates to determine whether one or two new DTC programmes were needed.
The Agency currently has three DTC programmes running under each of which it can borrow up to 7.5 billion guilders.
Its May programme has been fully used while some two thirds of the June and December programmes have been used up.
The April programme matured last Tuesday.
Dealers said in reply to questions that the new programme would probably mature at the end of July or August.
The June DTC programme was priced at 3.10 percent this morning and the December programme at 3.18 percent and dealers said business was thin at current price levels.
Call money rates rose on Thursday to their customary level of around 3.00 percent as forecast by dealers. Call was bid between 3.00 and 3.06 percent today.
On Tuesday call money rates suddenly plunged to 1.75 percent, but dealers predicted then that they would bounce back to the usual level on Thursday.
Dutch markets were closed on Wednesday due to the celebration of Queen's Day.
Other money market rates were unchanged with three-month deposits bid at 3.12 percent.
The guilder was slightly stronger at 112.485 per 100 marks against 112.50 on Tuesday.
